newsitem.title: ANGOLA: CHEVRON AIMS TO EXPAND ANGOLAN OPERATIONS.
newsitem.headline: CHEVRON AIMS TO EXPAND ANGOLAN OPERATIONS.

text.p: Chevron aims to expand its Angolan operations and increase crude oil production to 500,000 barrels per day over the next three years, according to the head of the company's Angolan subsidiary.
Mark Puckett, managing director of Cabinda Gulf Oil Company, Chevron's subsidiary in Angola, said in an interview last week the firm was interested in expanding from its offshore concession.
"We are very interested in expanding outside Block O," he said. The company had bid for Blocks 19, 21 and 22, far to the south of Cabinda, when they were put up earlier this year.
He declined to say what the company had bid for the blocks.
Other firms which also lodged offers with the government for the blocks were Texaco Inc , Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary and Brazil's Petrobras .

Cabinda Gulf Oil was also interested in expanding into ultra-deep water off Angola, Puckett said. This had not been offered for bid yet, but company officials and analysts said they expected the government to put blocks up later this year.
"We think the ultra-deep waters are the future of oil exploration in Angola," Puckett said, adding: "We have plenty of experience in deep water and I feel we can do a good job with it here."

Company projections for oil production for 1997 were about the same as last year at around 400,000 bpd and from 1998 the company hope for increased production which would reach around 500,000 bpd by the year 2000.
Puckett said the company also planned to increase spending on oil drilling, production and exploration.
"Last year we spent around $500 million and this year we will spend about $700 million. We will continue to spend in that range until at least 2000," he said.
The company was also expanding operations within Block O, with the Sanha and N'Dola fields in area C and the Lomba and Memba fields in area B due to begin producing soon.
This would mark the first time all three areas of Block O had been in production.

Cabinda Gulf Oil operates the 1.37 million acre offshore Cabinda concession. The Angolan state oil company Sonangol, the Italian oil company AGIP, and the French oil company Elf Aquitaine are shareholders in the concession.
Chevron also has a concession off neighbouring Zaire, operated with the U.S.-based Unical and the Japanese company Teikoku Oil Co Ltd , off the Zairean coast.
Chevron also is a partner with Elf in the Haute Mer Block off Congo.
Total Chevron production in the offshore areas of the three countries, known as the Congo River Basin, is over 600,000 bpd, Puckett said.
